subject: Quantix migration economics, deployment fees, and match request
messages:
From: Tim Jennings <tim.jennings@quantix.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@quantix.ai, Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@quantix.ai>
Date: 2027-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quantix evaluating Redwood — economics & migration questions

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this. We're running a short list evaluation of alternative inference providers and Redwood was recommended by our ML platform lead. I attached our current bill/usage snapshot (quantix_migration_costs.xlsx) so you can see our mix (high long-sequence chat + reranking traffic during peak hours).

A few things Procurement cares about up-front:
- Effective unit economics today (what we net after credits/commitments) — our incumbent is offering a blended rate that includes onboarding credits.
- Any migration/onboarding credit you can provide (we estimate ~8 weeks of ramp).
- Egress and log-retention fees during onboarding.
- Proof points for 99th percentile latency under our workload and fallback guarantees.

Can you run a quick migration/econ comparison and let us know whether Redwood can match or beat our incumbent effective price if we sign a 12-month commitment? If you can share a one-page comparison and a runbook for migration it will help speed procurement approval.

We'd like to schedule a short 30-min sync this week to walk numbers. Available windows: Wed 11–1 PDT or Thu 9–12 PDT.

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Jennings
Director of Platform Engineering | Quantix AI

+1 415-555-0192

Hi Tim — great to meet you via email.

Thanks for the spreadsheet — that helps a lot. Quick answer up-front: in most cases we can design a matched economics package when customers commit to a 12-month throughput or a dedicated pool; we also include a runbook and a pilot canary to validate latency SLAs before the full cutover.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) I’ll loop in Marissa (solutions) and Connor (implementation) to draft a 1-page comparison + a concise mutual action plan.
2) We can run a 2-week canary on a limited traffic slice (no charge) to validate 99p latency for your workload.
3) If you share the incumbent effective rate (after credits) we will attempt a straight match and show the break-even math.

I can take Wed 11:30 PDT for a 30-min call. Does that work?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Quantix — preliminary migration econ scenarios and runbook

Hi Tim — thanks for the data and context. I pulled together three discrete scenarios for Quantix based on the usage profile in your spreadsheet and our runtime characteristics (KV cache hit rates, batching sensitivity, and 95/99p token latency under multi-tenant vs dedicated). See the bullets below and the attached runbook (redwood_onboarding_runbook.pdf) for a high-level sequence of work.

Summary (numbers illustrative; final will be in a formal quote):
- Option A — Hosted, 12-mo commit (banded consumption):
  * Commitment: 12 months, stair-step consumption bands at 250/750/1,200 RPS equivalence.
  * Effective unit: ~$0.0038/token-equivalent (blended after a $60k onboarding credit amortized over 6 months).
  * Egress: waived first 90 days for onboarding traffic; standard egress thereafter.
  * SLA: 99p validated on canary; credit ladder (up to 10% of monthly fee) for sustained SLO misses beyond a defined correction window.

- Option B — Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs):
  * Commitment: 12 months reserved capacity.
  * Pricing: flat $85k/mo for a pool sized to your peak with on-demand burst credits.
  * Setup: one-time setup fee typically $18k — we will waive this for a 12-mo commitment.
  * Egress: included for first 90 days; then standard.

- Option C — Hybrid (dedicated critical routes + hosted for overflow):
  * Two-line pricing; blended effective unit price depends on traffic split.
  * Migration credit: $40k seat-based credit for professional services to accelerate model compatibility and kernel tuning.

Operational caveats & notes:
- The onboarding credit is amortized into the effective recurring economics; procurement often prefers it as a one-time credit (we can structure either way).
- Our pricing above assumes a standard termination clause; if Quantix requires a shorter rollback window or an early-exit carveout, we will need legal review which can change economics.
- We recommend a 2-week canary with traffic replay from production to validate KV cache hit and 99p latency under your exact prompt mix. That helps lock the SLA language into the contract.

Attachments included: redwood_onboarding_runbook.pdf (runbook stub) — contains the canary plan, test metrics, and cutover checklist.

If this looks directionally right, Vanessa and I will formalize a marked quote and a short mutual action plan for procurement.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Vanessa / Marissa — thank you for the thoughtful options and the runbook. Procurement will review the scenarios but a few immediate asks from legal/procurement before we move to an LOI:

- Can we see the 12-month NPV math in Excel (line by line) so our FP&A can sign off?
- Procurement will request a 30-day rollback window post-cutover (to revert traffic to incumbent if regressions are found). If Redwood can accommodate a 30-day rollback with a capped reversion fee (we proposed 10% of 1-month committed), that materially reduces procurement friction.
- Please confirm the onboarding credit treatment (one-time vs amortized) and whether egress waiver is 60 or 90 days in the final quote.

We plan to escalate to our CFO on Monday and will push for a decision contingent on the above. On the SLA/remedies — the credit ladder looks reasonable but Procurement may ask to codify an escalation path and faster remediation windows for P99 regressions.
